rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate all six peaks while limiting the time penalty and risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The elution window and critical resolutions will guide subsequent window trimming and slope or temperature changes.

The maximum CRF is already achieved, so test a shorter gradient to reduce analysis time while retaining full resolution. Keeping the solvent endpoints and temperature fixed isolates the effect of gradient steepness, with the current minimum resolution of 3.98 providing substantial margin.

Shorten the gradient another step while holding solvent endpoints and temperature fixed. The minimum resolution of 2.46 suggests that a four-minute gradient may preserve full resolution and the maximum CRF while further reducing analysis time.

The four-minute gradient retains the maximum CRF, but its first pair has little resolution margin. Raise temperature one step to test whether retention can be shortened without pushing that pair below R = 1.5.

Return to 40 C and trim the weak-solvent portion of the gradient by raising phi0 to 0.20, below the first peak’s estimated elution fraction of 0.27. This tests a shorter elution time with a shallower gradient slope, while retaining the strong endpoint for the last compound.

Test the shortest permitted gradient while lowering temperature to improve selectivity of the critical early pair, whose resolution worsened on heating. This explores a faster fully resolved method while preserving injection 5 as a maximum-score fallback.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to test further shortening at the minimum gradient duration. The shallower slope may help the critical early pair, but its narrow resolution margin makes this a boundary test against injection 6.

Increase phi0 one more grid step, since the previous increase improved the critical resolution while slightly shortening elution. This tests how far the initial solvent window can be trimmed before the early peaks become insufficiently retained.
Raise temperature one step to shorten retention while testing the improved early-pair resolution margin of 1.77. Keep phi0 fixed because the first peak is already close to the unretained region.

Test one further temperature step to locate the upper-temperature boundary for full resolution at the shortest gradient duration. The first pair may fall below 1.5; if so, injection 9 remains the fastest demonstrated maximum-CRF method.

Narrow the gradient window to reduce steepness and test whether full resolution can be restored at 35 C. The last peak may move into the final hold, but the modest endpoint reduction should keep the run comfortably below ten minutes.

Lower phi0 to retain the early pair more strongly and return to 30 C, where its selectivity was better. The slightly reduced endpoint tests whether a two-minute gradient can provide more resolution margin while keeping all six peaks well within ten minutes.

The maximum CRF is secured; now test a more robust two-minute method by combining lower temperature with a shallower gradient. Both changes should improve the critical early-pair resolution, while the last peak should remain comfortably within ten minutes.

Raise phi1 one step from injection 13 to accelerate the last peak during the final hold. The critical resolution should lie between the measured 1.85 at phi1 = 0.85 and 1.64 at phi1 = 0.95, preserving maximum CRF with some resolution margin.

Test the next starting-solvent step above injection 8 to locate the boundary where early-peak compression outweighs the benefit of a narrower gradient. This may shorten the fastest low-temperature method, but the first pair risks becoming insufficiently retained; injection 9 remains the fastest demonstrated maximum-CRF option.

Return to the fastest fully resolved starting fraction and temperature, then lower phi1 one step to seek additional resolution margin. This should modestly improve the critical pair relative to injection 9 while retaining a short run and maximum CRF.

Lower temperature one step from injection 16 to improve the limiting early-pair selectivity while keeping the minimum gradient duration. This tests a short, maximum-CRF alternative with more resolution margin than the fastest demonstrated method, injection 9.

Raise temperature one step from injection 13 to shorten its final-hold elution while using its 1.85 minimum resolution as margin. This tests whether the narrower gradient supports full resolution at 30 C without placing the first peak near the unretained region.

Increase phi0 one step from injection 18 to shorten elution while retaining its shallower gradient and favorable temperature. Neighboring methods suggest the critical pair should remain above 1.5, preserving the already-achieved maximum CRF.

Lower temperature one step from injection 19 to improve early-pair selectivity at the minimum gradient duration. This should provide additional resolution margin while preserving maximum CRF; injection 9 remains the fastest demonstrated fully resolved method.

With maximum CRF already secured, test a shallower two-minute gradient for additional resolution margin while keeping the first peak clearly retained. Relative to injection 13, the lower endpoint should improve the critical pair at the expense of modestly later final-hold elution.

Raise temperature one step from injection 21 to accelerate the last peak during the hold. Its minimum resolution of 1.97 provides margin for the expected loss in early-pair selectivity, making full resolution and maximum CRF likely.

Raise phi0 one step from injection 22 to trim initial retention while maintaining the shallower gradient. Nearby results suggest full resolution should be preserved; injection 9 remains the fastest demonstrated method at the maximum CRF.

Lower temperature one step from injection 23 to test additional early-pair resolution margin at the minimum gradient duration. This should retain maximum CRF, although injection 9 remains preferable when choosing strictly by shortest demonstrated fully resolved elution.

For the final injection, refine injection 6 by lowering phi1 one step to improve its marginal early-pair resolution while keeping the first peaks clearly retained. Maximum CRF is already secured; injection 9 remains the fastest demonstrated fully resolved method.
